Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), along with Representatives Pete Aguilar (D-Calif.), Jim Costa (D-Calif.), and Zoe Lofgren (D-Calif.), urged Secretary of Transportation Pete Buttigieg to approve the California High-Speed Rail Authority’s grant application for $536 million in federal funds. The project would support critical tunneling design work to advance construction from the Central Valley toward California’s largest population centers. The projected ridership for this new corridor would make it the most traveled intercity passenger service in the nation. “Advancing progress on the California Phase 1 Corridor is essential for enhancing our nation’s and California’s strategic transportation network investments,” wrote the lawmakers. “The Phase 1 Corridor aims to address climate concerns, promote health, improve access and connectivity, and boost economic vitality, while addressing current highway and rail capacity constraints.” “By preparing for future final design and construction of complex tunnels in this corridor, the Project will advance both state and federal goals to improve safety, expand economic strength and global competitiveness, address equity issues, and implement sustainability practices to confront climate change,” continued the lawmakers. “These investments will continue to support living wage jobs, provide small business opportunities, and equitably enhance the mobility of communities in need — including disadvantaged agricultural communities — all while reducing greenhouse gas emissions.” Background: The application for the California Phase 1 Corridor Tunneling Design — North and South — Project would support the next stage of design for the first two segments in a sequence of design sections, including a Bakersfield to Palmdale segment (South) and a Gilroy to Central Valley Wye segment (North). These segments have already been environmentally cleared. The FSP-National grant application is part of an ongoing federal-state partnership that has provided approximately $28.8 billion in funding for California High-Speed Rail, including $22 billion from state funds and $6.8 billion from federal funds. California has committed more funding for advanced electrified, 220 mph high-speed rail than any other state. Full text of the letter is available here and below: Dear Secretary Buttigieg: As members of the California Congressional delegation, we are writing to express our strong support for the California High-Speed Rail Authority’s (Authority) application for Fiscal Year 2024 funding from the Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail National Program for projects outside the Northeast Corridor (FSP-National). The Authority’s application for the California Phase 1 Corridor Tunneling Design – North and South – aims to support the next stage of design for the first two segments in a sequence of design sections that have been environmentally cleared: (1) Bakersfield to Palmdale (South); and (2) Gilroy to Central Valley Wye (North). The planned tunneling design work is essential for advancing the program from the current construction in the Central Valley toward the largest population centers of the State. The project development grant application is for $536 million that would be matched by state Cap-and-Trade funds of almost $134 million for a total project cost of roughly $670 million. The objective of the Project is to initiate the time-intensive and complex tunneling design work, achieving 30% design. This includes civil design, preliminary geotechnical studies, right-of-way design identification, and utility design. The scope of work in both sections involves detailed geotechnical investigations critical to completing the future final design of two long-lead-time, complex tunnel sections: (1) through the Tehachapi Mountains in Southern California; and (2) through the Pacheco Pass in the Diablo Mountain Range in Northern California. These tunnels will enable connections with other intercity passenger rail systems in the Southwest Region Corridor. In the South, California High-Speed Rail (CAHSR) will connect with two additional high-speed rail projects underway, the High Desert Corridor and Brightline West, as well as existing rail services, including Metrolink. In the North, CAHSR will connect with Caltrain and Altamont Commuter Express (ACE) rail services. The requested federal funds are needed to support areas of critical need in advancing the State’s first intercity passenger service operating at high speeds. The projected ridership for the California Phase 1 Corridor would make it the most traveled intercity passenger service in the nation. The Authority’s FSP-National grant application is part of an on-going federal-state partnership that, to-date, has provided approximately $28.8 billion in funding for California High-Speed Rail consisting of $22 billion (or 76%) from state funds and $6.8 billion (or 24%) from federal funds. California is the only state in the country to have committed this level of funding and advanced electrified, 220 mph high-speed rail this far. This historic federal-state partnership has also resulted in significant job and economic opportunities including: Creating more than 14,200 construction jobs since the start of high-speed rail construction through September 2024, with most of these jobs going to Central Valley residents and men and women from disadvantaged communities. Employing more than 860 small, disadvantaged, and disabled veteran businesses through August 2024. Yielding $7.0 billion in labor income and $18.0 billion in total economic output across the State from July 2006 through June 2023. Advancing progress on the California Phase 1 Corridor is essential for enhancing our nation’s and California’s strategic transportation network investments. The Phase 1 Corridor aims to address climate concerns, promote health, improve access and connectivity, and boost economic vitality, while addressing current highway and rail capacity constraints. By preparing for future final design and construction of complex tunnels in this corridor, the Project will advance both state and federal goals to improve safety, expand economic strength and global competitiveness, address equity issues, and implement sustainability practices to confront climate change. These investments will continue to support living wage jobs, provide small business opportunities, and equitably enhance the mobility of communities in need – including disadvantaged agricultural communities – all while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Please consider the enormous value and meaningful impact that FSP-National grant funding will provide to advancing CAHSR beyond the Central Valley. Sincerely, ###

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Cory Booker (D-N.J), along with U.S. Senators Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jeff Merkley (D-Oreg.), Ron Wyden (D-Oreg.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) sent a letter to President Biden urging him to take action under the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act (OCSLA) to protect unleased and at-risk areas of the Outer Continental Shelf from fossil fuel development. The Senators listed the ongoing and significant risks of offshore drilling, including catastrophic oil spills, abandoned wells, and hazardous drilling infrastructure that imperil coastal waters, local economies, and public health. Moreover, they stressed that expanding fossil fuel development would undermine climate commitments and expose American taxpayers to enormous environmental cleanup costs. “As you cement your legacy to be the nation’s greatest climate president, we urge you to use your authority designated under 12(a) of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act (OCSLA) to permanently withdraw unleased and at-risk areas of the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) from fossil fuel development. These coastal waters are too economically and ecologically important to drill, and our coastal communities deserve protection from the known dangers posed by offshore drilling,” the Senators wrote. “A large-scale withdrawal of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Eastern Gulf from fossil fuel development while maintaining the development of renewable energy solutions would provide durable protections for these critical areas,” the Senators wrote. “We have long fought for permanent protection from offshore oil and gas drilling for our communities, and for the clean energy future we need. We greatly appreciate your careful consideration of this letter and working to take action to protect our communities for generations to come,” the Senators concluded. To read the full text of the letter, click here.

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) voted against the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). He released the following statement: “The annual NDAA has long been a nonpartisan piece of legislation to ensure our national security. Partisan efforts to introduce policy riders to the bill that withhold make-or-break funds from our ally Ukraine, or undermine access to lifesaving health care for military families are unacceptable. “The NDAA should focus on protecting American troops and ensuring we have the resources to support our allies – not serve as a vehicle for the ideological issues of the day. “I have supported countless NDAA bills in the past and will continue to judge each defense bill on its merits. “And I will always do everything I can to support our servicemembers, our military readiness and might, and our national security. Inserting divisive policy riders into our defense authorization undermines that – and for that reason, I voted no.”

Washington, D.C. — Today, Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) joined ABC’s This Week with George Stephanopoulos to discuss President-elect Trump’s plan to pardon January 6th insurrectionists, his choices for cabinet picks, and more. Key Excerpts: On Trump’s promise to pardon January 6th insurrectionists First of all, that he could pardon people that beat police officers, gouged them, bear sprayed them. But also, even beyond that, just the general message it would send, George, that his first pardons are going to go to people who saw it through the use of violence at the Capitol to stop the peaceful transfer of power that played some role in that. Really? That’s who he wants to pardon? The American people, I think, voted for him in part because they wanted something done about crime. Not because they wanted to see him pardoning criminals, attacking the government. They want something done about fentanyl. They want something done about California. Smash-and-grab robberies. This is not what they had in mind. Not political revenge, not rewarding people who participated in an insurrection to stop the transfer of power. On the nomination of Kash Patel to lead the FBI Well, let me just say, with respect to some of the nominees, like Kash Patel, this is someone, in my view, who is not qualified to be FBI director and someone who claimed, for example, that he wanted to shut down FBI headquarters, early in his tenure and open a museum to the deep state. So this is a conspiracy theorist. It’s also someone, I think, who demonstrated, sadly, a principle of the first Trump administration. And that is, you rise to the level of your sycophancy. And the bigger the sycophant, the higher you rise. He’s risen pretty high. But that’s not what we’re looking for in an FBI director. On the dangers of Tulsi Gabbard as director of National Intelligence It is a concern to me. I have a couple concerns with Tulsi Gabbard. The first is a complete lack of experience, never worked in an intelligence agency, never even served on the intelligence committee. There is a very steep learning curve in trying to understand what the intelligence systems do, the role and the interaction between them, not something you want learning on the job. But also —and this gets to the point about her comments about Bashar al-Assad or her echoing of Kremlin talking points about the origin of the war in Ukraine— you want someone with good judgment in that position because they may very well be whispering in the ear of the president, this is how we should interpret this intelligence, these are the steps that we should take. This is our friend, this is our enemy. Someone who had shown that kind of poor judgment is not necessarily someone you want advising this president. Watch the full video of the interview here .

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), members of the Senate Judiciary Committee, applauded the confirmation of three federal judges to fill vacancies on U.S. District Courts in California. The recently confirmed judges include Judge Cynthia Valenzuela to the U.S. District Court for the Central District and Judge Noël Wise to the Northern District. Additionally, Judge Anne Hwang was confirmed to the California Central District on December 2nd, prior to Senator Schiff joiningthe United States Senate. “Cynthia Valenzuela and Noël Wise are extremely well qualified, dedicated public servants. They will make outstanding jurists. I was proud to support them — and I congratulate them on their confirmation to the bench,” said Senator Schiff. “These three confirmations to California federal District Courts are a product of Senate Democrats working around the clock alongside President Biden to identify and confirm record numbers of highly qualified and diverse judges,” said Senator Padilla. “Judges Hwang, Valenzuela, and Wise possess a wealth of judicial and litigation experience, and I am confident they will continue to serve the people of California with honor.” “One of the most critical duties in representing the people of California in the Senate is ensuring access to fair and equitable justice,” said former California Senator Laphonza Butler. “I applaud the Senate’s confirmation of Judges Anne Hwang, Noël Wise, and Cynthia Valenzuela – all highly-qualified women who bring a wealth of experience to federal bench. By confirming these exceptional jurists, the Senate has taken important steps to deliver on the fundamental promise of justice for all.” Judge Cynthia Valenzuela: U.S. District Court for the Central District of California Judge Cynthia Valenzuela has been a judge on the California State Bar Court in Los Angeles since her appointment by the California Supreme Court in 2016. Previously, Judge Valenzuela worked as the Criminal Justice Act Supervising Attorney for the Central District of California in Los Angeles from 2011 to 2016 and as the head of national litigation at the Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund in Los Angeles from 2006 to 2011. Before that, Judge Valenzuela served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California from 2000 to 2006; as a trial attorney in the U.S. Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division in Washington, D.C. from 1998 to 2000; and as a Special Assistant at the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights in Los Angeles from 1995 to 1998. She received her J.D. from the University of California at Los Angeles School of Law in 1995 and her B.A. from the University of Arizona in 1991. Judge Noël Wise: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California Judge Noël Wise has been a judge on the Superior Court of California in Alameda County since 2014, and a supervising judge since 2019. From 2021 to 2022, she served as a Judge Pro Tem for the California Second District Court of Appeal. She previously practiced law as a partner at Wise Gleicher in Alameda, California from 2006 to 2014 after working as in-house counsel for Pacific Gas and Electric Company in San Francisco from 2004 to 2006. From 2002 to 2004, Judge Wise was of counsel at Stoel Rives LLP in San Francisco. Before entering private practice, Judge Wise served as a trial attorney in the U.S. Department of Justice, Environmental and Natural Resources Division in Washington, D.C. from 1994 to 2002, where she entered through the Honors Program. From 1997 to 1998, she was detailed to serve as an Assistant United States Attorney in the U.S Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California. Judge Wise served as a law clerk for Justice Harry Lee Anstead on the Florida Fourth District Court of Appeals from 1993 to 1994. She received her J.S.M. from Stanford Law School in 2002; her J.D., cum laude, from Nova Southeastern University Law School in 1993; and her B.S. from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, in 1989. Judge Anne Hwang: U.S. District Court for the Central District of California Judge Anne Hwang has been a judge on the Superior Court of California in Los Angeles County since 2019. Prior to taking the bench, Judge Hwang served as a Deputy Federal Public Defender in the Office of the Federal Public Defender for the Central District of California from 2006 to 2018, becoming Chief Deputy Federal Public Defender in 2018. Before that, Judge Hwang worked as a litigation associate at Irell & Manella LLP from 2002 to 2006. She received her J.D. from the University of Southern California Law School in 2002 and her B.A. from Cornell University in 1997. ###

Washington, D.C. — Today, Adam Schiff was sworn in to serve as the next United States Senator from California. Schiff will now fulfill the rest of former Senator Dianne Feinstein’s term and issued the following statement after taking the oath of office: “I am deeply grateful for the opportunity to serve all Californians as their next United States Senator. My family came to the Golden State when I was a child in the hope of finding a strong economy, safe neighborhoods, and good schools. And we found all that we could hope for in each of these respects. “Today our state faces significant challenges in the form of a very high cost of living and incomes that have simply not kept pace. In the Senate, I will do everything I can to bring people together to tackle our housing crisis, create an economy that works for everyone, and bring down rising costs from health care to childcare. “I will be a tireless advocate for Californians in every part of the state and work across the aisle to deliver on day one. California is the creative hub of the world with a tremendous resource in its brilliant, creative, and hardworking people, and a natural beauty that is the envy of the world. I will work with Democrats, Republicans, and Independents to help our state and our families succeed. “At the same time, I will not shrink from my duty to defend our democracy and will vigorously protect the rights and freedoms of the American people and the people of California. “I recognize that I stand on the shoulders of giants. Former Senator Dianne Feinstein leaves behind an extraordinary legacy of courage and effectiveness. Nobody can ever fill her immense shoes but I will continue to be inspired by her example. I am so thankful to Senator Barbara Boxer for believing in me, for her extraordinary environmental stewardship, and her own profound legacy in the Senate. “And, of course, I am profoundly grateful to Speaker Nancy Pelosi, my mentor, friend – and the greatest Speaker of all time – for her support and encouragement at every step of my career in Congress. I am also grateful for Senator Alex Padilla’s friendship and look forward to continuing to collaborate closely with him on behalf of the people of our state. And, finally, I want to thank Senator Laphonza Butler for her impressive service. I look forward to what she accomplishes next. “Finally, I want to thank my wife, Eve, our two beautiful children, and the loving encouragement of my parents, Ed and Sherrill Schiff, of beloved memory. “The work ahead of us will not be easy – nothing worth doing ever is. But my promise is to work every day to deliver results, and make California’s future brighter for all of us in this Golden State.” ###

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.), both members of the Senate Judiciary Committee, released the following statement reacting to the introduction of the Judicial Understaffing Delays Getting Emergencies Solved (JUDGES) Act : “We appreciate the efforts by Senators Coons and Young to create new judicial seats that are sorely needed, and we have supported previous versions of this bill. However, the latest version of the bill now includes a poison pill provision to lay the groundwork for a split of the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals — long the dream of arch conservatives — which is unacceptable to us. “The Ninth Circuit operates efficiently, and this court’s opinions are deeply respected and crucial on issues related to immigration, the environment, technology, civil liberties and much more. But for years, the circuit has been targeted by conservative legal activists trying to weaken its influence and attack its reasoning. This provision seeks to help legitimize those harmful efforts under the pretext of judicial efficiency. “We appreciate the willingness of Senator Coons and Senator Young to work with us on this issue and look forward to continued conversations moving forward, but we want to be clear that we cannot support this bill while it includes this troubling provision.” ###

The DEATH BETS Act is the first bill regulating prediction markets to pass in the Senate in the 119 th Congress Washington, D.C. — Last night, the U.S. Senate unanimously passed U.S. Senator Adam Schiff’s (D-Calif.) and John Curtis’ (R-Utah), DEATH BETS Act , legislation to explicitly prohibit any Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)-registered entity from listing any contract that references terrorism, assassination, war, United States Armed Forces military operations, or an individual’s death. Schiff, a member of the Senate Agriculture Committee, first introduced this bill in March 2026. Representative Mike Levin (D-Calif.-49) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives. Senator Schiff delivered remarks on the Senate floor moments before the bill passed and was joined by Senator Curtis. Watch his full speech HERE. “Betting on war and death jeopardizes our national security by creating a perverse environment in which violence is incentivized and insiders are allowed to profit off privileged or classified information. There is no justification for gambling on lives, or public benefit to be derived by such a market. With my bill, Congress is making it clear today that these death bets should be unlawful,” said Senator Schiff. “No one should be able to wager on terrorism, war, or the death of another human being,” said Senator Curtis . “There is a fundamental difference between legitimate financial markets and gambling on human suffering. The DEATH BETS Act draws a clear moral line by prohibiting these types of wagers on federally regulated exchanges.” Under the Commodity Exchange Act , the CFTC currently has the authority to prohibit war, terrorism, and assassination contracts from being listed if they are determined by the Commission to be contrary to the public interest. Whether or not these contracts are in the public interest is at the discretion of the CFTC. At a time when CFTC Chair Selig has indicated that he will rewrite the rules on prediction markets, the CFTC can no longer be granted this discretion. This bill will unequivocally ban these contracts. According to public reporting, there have been numerous cases this year in which individuals were suspected to have traded on prediction markets to profit from inside information related to war and U.S. Armed Services actions. Lawmakers have previously raised the alarm to the CFTC on these “death contracts” being offered on offshore exchanges, such as on whether or not Artemis II would explode, Maduro would be removed from power, or the Ukrainian town of Myrnohad would be captured by Russian forces. The DEATH BETS Act specifically would: Codify a prohibition on war, assassination, and terrorism contracts. Explicitly prohibit contracts that involve an individual’s death, which is not currently referenced in the Commodity Exchange Act . The full text of the bill is available here. Read the full transcript of his remarks as delivered below: Senator Adam Schiff: Mr. President, I’m here today to urge the Senate to pass legislation that I’m proud to lead along with Senator John Curtis, the DEATH BETS Act . Over the last two years, the rapid growth prediction markets has allowed users to gamble on just about anything. Just this year, we’ve seen these markets offer wagers on whether the Artemis II mission and its four astronauts would explode. It created a market on whether Nicolas Maduro would be removed from power in Venezuela. It even offered a potential profit for those who could correctly predict whether a Ukrainian town of Myrnohrad would be captured by Russia. In many cases, these contracts offered were offered in contravention of state and Tribal law. They create rampant opportunities for insider trading, and perhaps worst of all, they are offered with no regard for national security and, in far too many cases, even basic morality. These markets are operating in a wild west, desperately in need of regulation and guardrails. Today, we have the opportunity to put into place a very simple rule: the first building block to create one of those guardrails. Our bill prohibits prediction markets from offering contracts on war, military operations, and death, Betting and profiting off of death, both in tragedy and in war, is immoral and ought to be unlawful. Indeed, many of us believe it already is. But the regulators at CFTC, or in this case, regulator, is not only hands off. He’s acting as the legal infantry for the industry, attempting to preempt state laws and challenging them whenever his agency is unsuccessful. As a result, the CFTC has created a system with the most perverse incentives that would reward betting on a mass casualty event. A market that one could easily imagine would actually encourage lethal events and jeopardize our national security for the right amount of money. It’s a whole new version of the very idea of a contract kill. Take the real-life example we’ve seen on these platforms: people placing bets on wildfires, wagering on how devastating they could be; people placing bets on every twist and turn in the war with Iran, sometimes with inside information, motivated by the same underlying principle of financial markets and gaming conventions, the possibility of profit. But these are not regulated financial markets; they’re not seen by the administration as sports betting or gambling, even though such illegal practices are widespread and the subject of yet another bill that Senator Curtis and I are leading. There’s no justification for gambling on lives or public benefit to be derived by such a market. It’s dangerous and it’s wrong. In the absence of real leadership and enforcement at the CFTC, it’s time for Congress to step in and fix this problem. With our bill, Congress is making clear that these bets should be illegal once and for all. Simply put, the legislation we are enacting today is a targeted fix of a single pressing problem. The sole purpose of the DEATH BETS Act is to make clear that betting on war, death, military operations, and similar circumstances is unlawful. But we also want to make clear that the legislation has no effect whatsoever on pending litigation regarding whether sports contracts offered by prediction markets qualify as swaps or other derivatives under federal law, or on whether federal derivatives laws preempt state gaming and consumer protection laws regarding such sports contracts. We’ve included a rule of construction in the DEATH BETS Act designed to make this crystal clear. Per that rule, no part of this bill will affect the permissibility of any sports contracts or similar agreements. If sports contracts are impermissible under federal or state law today, as I, and many others believe they are, it will remain impermissible after this legislation is enacted. We are aware that there is active litigation across the country on swaps and preemption issues. Nothing in the DEATH BETS Act should have any effect on those lawsuits, and it would be improper to draw any inference from this bill that other federal statutes or regulations should be interpreted in a particular way, or that Congress has expressed any intent on how the issues in litigation should be decided. Nor should the DEATH BETS Act be construed as providing the CFTC with authority to authorize or regulate sports contracts on prediction markets. The CFTC has no expertise with respect to gaming. The states and Tribes have long served as the nation’s gaming regulators, and nothing Congress is doing today displaces that traditional state and Tribal authority. Indeed, the CFTC’s recent actions to attempt to assist prediction markets in litigation confirm that the CFTC has strayed far outside its authority. Sports contracts are sports bets in disguise. The CFTC’s job is to promote fair competition and market efficiency, not to serve as a nationwide sports betting regulator. This bill is a commonsense step, and merely the first to rein in a runaway prediction market regulation that violates state law and Tribal sovereignty, common sense, and our values. I want to again thank my colleague Senator Curtis for his advocacy and leadership, not just on this bill but on a broader issue, and I would be proud to yield to Senator Curtis. ###

Washington, D.C . – Momentum continues to grow for the bipartisan and bicameral Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act , legislation to create a federal film tax incentive with the addition of new bipartisan Senate support, key stakeholders, and 60+ new cosponsors in the House of Representatives. The legislation was introduced in September in the Senate by U.S. Senators Tim Scott (R-S.C.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), and by Representatives Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas-1), Linda Sánchez (D-Calif- 38), Brian Jack (R-Ga-3), and Laura Friedman (D-Calif-30) in the U.S. House of Representatives. The new Senate cosponsors include: Senators Chris Coons (D-Del.), Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), Katie Britt (R-Ala.) and Dick Durbin (D-Ill.). The legislation is also cosponsored by Senators John Cornyn (R-Texas.), Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Tim Sheehy (R-Montana), Mark Warner (D-Va.), and Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.). The introduction of the bill follows years of advocacy to create a nationwide tax credit for film and television production, a push recently echoed by President Donald Trump. “The bipartisan coalition for our bill continues to grow, and I’m proud of the support we have gained from members of Congress representing different states across the country. This bill will create new jobs, boost our local economies, and stop the offshoring of film and TV production from leaving the United States, and it’s time we make this much-needed incentive a reality. Given the support from Republicans and Democrats in both chambers and the president, we can get this legislation across the finish line,” said Senator Schiff. “Film and television production supports good-paying jobs and drives investment in communities far beyond Hollywood, including in states like Alabama,” said Senator Britt. “But for too long, countries have used aggressive incentives to lure American production companies, and the jobs that come with them, overseas. This bipartisan legislation would level the playing field and reward companies for bringing production back home. I’m proud to join my colleagues in this effort.” “American film and television are some of our most successful cultural exports and engines of our economy,” said Senator Coons. “It’s worth investing in that power and creativity. I’m glad so many others from Democrats to Republicans to stakeholders agree, and we should keep working to move this bill forward.” “American film and television productions support good-paying jobs, creative talent, and economic growth in communities across the country. We should be doing everything we can to ensure that these productions stay in the United States rather than move overseas to take advantage of more competitive incentives,” said Senator Durbin. “This legislation will help support American workers, strengthen our economy, and keep these jobs here at home.” “North Carolina has a rich history in film and television production, and we should be doing everything we can to ensure that legacy continues,” said Senator Tillis . “This bipartisan legislation will help incentivize production companies to bring their projects and investments back to the United States, while supporting hardworking industry professionals and creating economic opportunities for North Carolina workers and businesses.” “The bipartisan support behind this bill is there for a reason. The need is real. Members of both parties have watched jobs in their districts move overseas. Momentum is on our side, and we need to strike while the iron is hot by passing this bill before the end of the year,” said Congresswoman Linda Sánchez. “Republicans and Democrats from every corner of the country keep signing on, because this is a national jobs issue with a commonsense fix. Crews in California, Georgia, Texas, New York, New Jersey, and beyond all want the same thing: to keep this industry in America instead of watching the work move overseas. I’m grateful to every partner who has joined this fight, and I’m ready to get a national film tax credit across the finish line,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman. Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works and Ranking Member of the Fisheries, Water, and Wildlife Subcommittee, issued the following statement after voting against the permitting reform legislation on the Senate floor: “We desperately need permitting reform to build out new infrastructure, bring costs down, and bring new, renewable sources of energy online. But it needs to be the right kind of regulatory reform, not oil and gas development masquerading as reform. And throughout the negotiation process, I have made my priorities clear: to bring down energy costs through new clean energy development, to lower emission rates, to support and protect tribal sovereignty, to stop the administration from attacking American clean energy projects, and to ensure that any permitting reform legislation cannot be weaponized by this or any future administration to single out states for adverse treatment and provide giveaways to the oil and gas industries. This is why I submitted more than a dozen amendments for consideration in both the managers’ package and on the Senate floor that would have made the bill better. “As it stands, this bill achieves some critically important priorities, but falls short on others. I appreciate the bipartisan work on this bill and the support of the 36 Senators who joined me in pushing for an amendment that would have struck the legislation’s changes to the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA). In the new Congress, there will be a lot of opportunity to improve protections for tribal sovereignty, and I will continue consulting with California’s tribal leaders to ensure their voices are heard in the halls of Congress. “I strongly believe we need permitting reform and to build new infrastructure quickly and efficiently. But I also believe that this can be done in a way that does not needlessly degrade clean water, endanger wildlife, or disrespect tribal nations. And for those fundamental reasons, I opposed the bill. It is my hope that when this bill is again considered in the new Congress, that a Democrat majority can pass a more balanced work product that accomplishes all of these objectives.” ###

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) released the following statement after the Senate voted to block a War Powers Resolution calling for an end to the Iran War: “It has been nearly nine months since this administration launched an unauthorized war in Iran. 23 servicemembers have lost their lives and many more have been injured. And for nine months, Americans have been left bearing the cost in higher gas prices, food prices, and so much more. “Americans sent a clear message in the midterm elections: they want an end to the war. While we had bipartisan support in today’s vote, it was not enough. In the new Congress, we will change that.” Background : Senator Schiff, along with U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-Va.) and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), have forced numerous votes in the Senate to end the war against Iran. This was the Senate’s 15th vote to force an end to the war through a War Powers Resolution. ###

Schiff: “Policymakers should make clear that Congress and American taxpayers won’t act as its fail-safe should this industry falter under its own immense weight.” Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) penned an op-ed in the Wall Street Journal highlighting concerns that if an AI industry bubble bursts it has the potential to destabilize the economy. The Senator says that Congress must make clear that American taxpayers will not act as a fail-safe to bail out the industry or its investors. Schiff notes: “This may be the biggest economic gamble in American history, and policymakers should make clear that Congress and American taxpayers won’t act as its fail-safe should this industry falter under its own immense weight… If these enormous bets fail, Big Tech and Wall Street billionaires will no doubt turn to Washington for emergency rescue, a path unfortunately well-trodden by corporate giants before them. But the risk should be borne by these companies and their investors, not working families.” In the op-ed, Schiff points to AI’s explosive buildout being financed by opaque debt structures and special-purpose vehicles, as companies are borrowing capital from an increasingly consolidated group of investors and lenders while free cash flow is declining. Schiff says: “The billionaire investors may be taking this gamble with the assumption that as in 2008, they will be bailed out for failed investments and corporate risk-taking. Congressional majorities should be clear: We won’t bail them out.” Read the full op-ed below: Wall Street Journal Op-Ed: No AI Company Is Too Big to Fail By Adam B. Schiff Our nation is in the midst of what will be one of the largest economic transformations in human history, driven by rapid advances in artificial intelligence and the corporations fueling their growth. This technology has boundless potential to enhance our lives and expand our individual and collective capacity. But as the turmoil around Nvidia reminds us, this swift and massive investment also carries significant risk that an industry downturn or a bubble could destabilize the American economy. In the first six days of the scandal involving Nvidia and its former CEO, the sector lost $500 billion in value. Given the risks to our economy and investors, Congress must make sure that industry understands this: No company is too big to fail, and in the event of a financial collapse of the tech sector, there will be no taxpayer-funded bailout. The AI industry, after less than five years of market power, is already estimated to represent 3.6% of our nation’s economy. But much of its explosive build-out is financed by an opaque debt structure and expectations of increasing profitability. This may be the biggest economic gamble in American history, and policymakers should make clear that Congress and American taxpayers won’t act as its fail-safe should this industry falter under its own immense weight. This year alone, AI will see nearly $1 trillion invested in its continued expansion. If these enormous bets fail, Big Tech and Wall Street billionaires will no doubt turn to Washington for emergency rescue, a path unfortunately well-trodden by corporate giants before them. But the risk should be borne by these companies and their investors, not working families. We have seen this movie before. In the early 2000s, there were warning signs that the housing market had taken on immense systemic risk, which had the potential to drag down our entire economy. The American people and Congress were told by top bank and mortgage lending executives, as well as the Treasury secretary and Federal Reserve chairman, that the subprime mortgage market was contained from the rest of the financial system and that the economy was healthy. That was catastrophically wrong. In 2008 those same officials begged Congress to forgive their error and pass an industry-wide bailout, while our nation was on the brink of a financial calamity. The result, reluctantly approved by Democrats and Republicans in Congress amid the crisis, gave executives who gambled with America’s economy billions of dollars to forgive their gambling debt while the American people were plunged into the worst economic recession since the Great Depression. No executives were charged with criminal wrongdoing. The average American family saw its wealth decline by a third from 2007 to 2010, with 1 in 4 households losing 75 cents of every dollar in its savings, home equity and net worth. Even as the economy began to stabilize, middle-class wealth remained stagnant and wages flat while the wealthiest Americans quickly made up what they had lost in the worst years. This must not happen again. As venture-capital firms and trillion-dollar companies are increasingly taking on more debt to build out AI without the financial certainty that it will pay off—and with the added danger that AI companies will be held liable for the damage their agents do in the wild—they should do so understanding that this risk won’t be borne by others. Now is the time to right-size the risk and debt, before a crisis. This is true not only of the big banks and investment houses, but also of the regional banks and pension funds. The collapse of Silicon Valley Bank demonstrated the fragility of the system when the financial liquidity of even midsize firms is threatened. Regulators should take precautions now, not after the fact. Big Tech hyperscaling companies used to be able to finance their data-center infrastructure build-outs from the profits of their existing businesses. But as they race to invest massive sums they don’t have on hand to project confidence in their businesses, these companies are borrowing capital from an increasingly consolidated group of investors and lenders while their free cash flow is declining. Smaller infrastructure companies are even more leveraged, borrowing billions against GPUs, data centers and anticipated future lease payments. Banks, private credit funds, insurers and pension funds are also financing this expansion, often through complicated corporate structures and special-purpose vehicles that obscure who ultimately holds the risk. The billionaire investors may be taking this gamble with the assumption that as in 2008, they will be bailed out for failed investments and corporate risk-taking. Congressional majorities should be clear: We won’t bail them out. On Election Day the American people rejected the corruption and special treatment that exists in our current politics across party lines, under which billionaires and industry giants get sweetheart deals at the expense of everyone else. We should listen to the message voters sent us. Mr. Schiff, a Democrat, is a U.S. senator from California. ###

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced the Sunlight on SuperPACs Act of 2026, legislation to require federal election campaign ads paid for by Super PACs to disclose the name and dollar amount contributed to that SuperPAC by its top three major donors of $5,000 or more. By providing voters with more information on the funders of election ads, they will be able to make more informed decisions about the content of those ads. “As each election cycle in recent history has shown us, Super PAC spending on campaign advertisements can have enormous influence, so it’s crucial that Americans know when special interests or corporations are funding these ads. Anonymous and unrestricted spending by Super PACs is dangerous and weakens our democracy, and it’s time for Congress to rein in the lack of transparency that exists in our campaign finance system. This bill is a step in the right direction so that voters can make more informed decisions at the polls,” said Senator Schiff. Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (D-Ohio-09) and Congressman Kevin Mullin (D-Calif.-15) introduced this legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives. In the Senate, this bill is cosponsored by Senators Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) and Mazie Hirono (D- Hawaii.). The legislation is endorsed by Citizens for Responsible Ethics in Washington (CREW), Democracy Defenders Action (DDA), End Citizens United (ECU), Issue One, and Public Citizen. “At a time when so many Super PACs use fake names and paperwork games to disguise who’s paying for their ads, voters need real information so they can make informed decisions. The Sunlight on SuperPACs Act will give voters the tools they need to evaluate the credibility of campaign ads by seeing who’s really behind them. We applaud Senator Schiff for championing this innovative way to cut through campaign funding schemes and empower voters,” said Jon Golinger, Democracy Advocate, Public Citizen. “Voters have a right to know who’s trying to sway their vote, but too often, our political system lets special interests hide behind misleadingly named organizations. The Sunlight on SuperPACs Act gives voters the information they need to understand who funds the political ads they see, building on measures that have passed with cross-partisan support in places such as Alaska, Arizona, and California. This bill would increase trust and accountability in our elections, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle should support it,” said Issue One Founder and CEO Nick Penniman. “Current loopholes in super PAC disclosure laws have led to anonymous donors making record breaking donations with little to no transparency provided to voters on the source of the funding. Loopholes like this have allowed dark money to influence US elections and allow elected officials to escape accountability for who they are accepting money from. Meaningful campaign finance reform is long overdue. CREW is proud to endorse the Sunlight on Super PACs Act sponsored by Senator Adam Schiff and Representatives Marcy Kaptur and Kevin Mullin, and we urge Congress to pass this important legislation,” said Debra Perlin, Vice President for Policy at CREW. “All Americans deserve to know who is trying to influence their voices and their votes. However, when billionaires and corporate special interests spend millions of dollars in secret political money, voters are too often left in the dark. We commend Senator Schiff for introducing the Sunlight on SuperPACs Act to ensure Americans get the transparency they deserve, and we urge Congress to quickly consider this bill,” said Virginia Canter, Ethics and Anticorruption Chief Counsel and Director with Democracy Defenders Action. In today’s electoral system, Super PACs can spend an unlimited amount of money to support or oppose political candidates, and they are not limited in how much money they can accept from donors. While they cannot give money directly to candidates or their campaigns, these organizations can have tremendous amounts of influence on elections through spending money on advertising and organizing. The Sunlight on SuperPACs will give voters information about the source of campaign ad funding in real-time, following the example of successful state and local disclosure initiatives, including an initiative enacted by voters in California. Lawmakers Want to Know How the Trump Administration Extorted and Used Other Law Firms and Whether They Took on Work Advising on Trump’s Vanity Projects Like Kennedy Center Renaming, Triumphal Arch Washington, D.C. — Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.-08), Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) demanded records from nine law firms after their investigation uncovered that the law firm Kirkland & Ellis LLP (Kirkland) provided at least $11.8 million in free legal services to federal agencies and federal entities after being threatened with an Equal Employment Opportunity Commission investigation and retributive Executive Orders that the Trump Administration had leveled against other firms. The probe also uncovered that Kirkland balked at helping the Trump Administration rename the Kennedy Center and build the President’s triumphal arch, raising questions about whether other firms that struck deals with the Administration took on those projects. The lawmakers sent follow-up letters to Latham & Watkins LLP (Latham) ; Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP (Simpson Thacher); Willkie Farr & Gallagher LLP (Willkie); Sullivan & Cromwell LLP (S&C); Hogan Lovells Cadwalader LLP (Cadwalader); Allen Overy Shearman Sterling US LLP (A&O Shearman); Milbank LLP (Milbank); Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP (Paul, Weiss); and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP (Skadden Arps). “We have recently received substantial and profoundly troubling information that this corrupt bargain went much further than originally understood. Kirkland & Ellis LLP provided at least $11.8 million in free legal services to numerous federal agencies and entities engaged in questionable activities, including approximately $4 million to the U.S. Department of Commerce, $2.2 million to the U.S. Department of Defense, $1.6 million to the U.S. Postal Service, $2 million to the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, and $1.8 million to represent an investment entity negotiated between the Trump Administration and Japan to create a $550 billion slush fund. The Trump Administration also unsuccessfully tried to involve Kirkland & Ellis in work supporting the President’s political vanity projects, such as the renaming of the Kennedy Center or supporting the illegal construction of his triumphal arch in Washington, D.C.— raising serious questions of whether other firms acceded to these demands,” the lawmakers wrote. The lawmakers received this information from Kirkland just two days after the November midterm elections. Since April 2025, the lawmakers have repeatedly demanded answers about the ten firms’ dubious multimillion-dollar deals with President Trump. However, to date, the vast majority of the firms still have yet to provide any substantive answers or turn over a single responsive document. The lawmakers renewed their demands for all outstanding records about the Executive Order and directed the firms to prioritize records of requests for free or discounted legal services from the White House, any executive branch agency, or any public or private associate of the President. They are seeking the nature of each request, who made it, what services each firm agreed to provide, and the hours and billable value of any work performed. Today’s letters are the latest salvo in an investigation Ranking Members Raskin and Blumenthal launched in April 2025 into Trump’s unprecedented official coercion of major law firms and the deals firms struck to avoid retaliation . Joined by Sen. Schiff, they subsequently scrutinized firms’ free legal work for the Commerce Department , sought records of Epshteyn’s role in Kirkland’s deal and pressed Skadden over potential conflicts involving its work for Intel and the Commerce Department . In October, the lawmakers rejected Kirkland’s claims of privilege and renewed their demands for records on its $125 million deal after the firm failed to produce a single responsive document and refused to meet with congressional staff. The lawmakers warned that they will use every tool at their disposal to pursue the investigation in this Congress and the next. As the initial phases of this investigation make clear, the President of the United States abused the power of the federal government to extract nearly $1 billion in free legal services from some of the nation’s largest law firms. Worse, the agreements announced on Truth Social effectively made the President the sole judge of whether those firms were complying with their obligations—putting these firms at the political mercy of the Administration and the personal mercy of the President, driving major firms away from both existing and potential clients and causes that could put them at odds with the mercurial shakedown artist in the White House. For people and communities who rely on pro bono lawyers to defend their rights, that could mean facing the full power and intensifying fury of the federal government alone.
