Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) along with Representatives Juan Vargas (D-Calif.-52), Sara Jacobs (D-Calif.-51), Mike Levin (D-Calif.-49), and Scott Peters (D-Calif.-50) demanded answers from the Trump Administration after an eight-year-old Haitian child who lost Temporary Protected Status earlier this year was taken into federal custody after an immigration check-in in San Diego. “An ICE officer reportedly invoked the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 while taking him into custody, apparently placing the child in restraints and separating him from the person who brought him for his hearing. Video footage appears to show the use of restraints on a child who seemed to pose no threat to those around him, raising serious questions about the handling of this incident,” wrote the lawmakers. “We express concerns about the basis for this action and the harm it may cause a young child who appeared for his required hearing.” “With this letter, we emphasize that the safety and well-being of children and families in San Diego County must remain the highest priority,” the lawmakers continued. “We also request confirmation on the child’s whereabouts, whether his family is aware of his location, and what steps your agencies are taking to ensure he can be reunited with them.” Read the full letter here and below. Dear Secretary Mullin and Secretary Kennedy, We write to express deep concerns regarding reports that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained an eight-year-old Haitian child at a scheduled immigration hearing in San Diego, California, on November 5, 2026. An ICE officer reportedly invoked the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 while taking him into custody, apparently placing the child in restraints and separating him from the person who brought him for his hearing. Video footage appears to show the use of restraints on a child who seemed to pose no threat to those around him, raising serious questions about the handling of this incident. We express concerns about the basis for this action and the harm it may cause a young child who appeared for his required hearing before the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR). Our September 22, 2026, letter concerning ICE enforcement activity around school and educational institutions addressed the fear and disruption these actions cause in our communities. House Members of the San Diego congressional delegation also wrote to both the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Department of Education on October 14, 2025, highlighting concerns from twenty-five San Diego County school district superintendents. The superintendents requested DHS to adopt clear consistent enforcement policies and coordination between the departments to keep schools safe places to learn. This reported detention underscores those concerns. Following this third-grade student’s detention, San Diego Unified School District reportedly sent crisis counselors to Fay Elementary School to support his classmates, who expressed fear and distress. The effects of this action extend far beyond one child and his family. With this letter, we emphasize that the safety and well-being of children and families in San Diego County must remain the highest priority. We will continue to monitor this situation closely and expect timely updates on the child’s well-being and your agencies’ response to these concerns. We also request confirmation on the child’s whereabouts, whether his family is aware of his location, and what steps your agencies are taking to ensure he can be reunited with them. We ask that you promptly review this child’s case and give it your full and fair consideration based on its merits, consistent with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Please provide our offices with an update regarding your findings from this review by December 1, 2026. ###

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works and Ranking Member of the Fisheries, Water, and Wildlife Subcommittee, issued the following statement after voting against the motion to proceed to the permitting reform legislation on the Senate floor: “The need for a permitting reform package has only grown in the past decade, as bureaucracy has stymied the development of vital projects from clean energy to housing that could lower costs. And I appreciate the work done by Senators Whitehouse and Heinrich to negotiate a bipartisan agreement, as a lasting solution can only be reached by reaching across the aisle. In particular, the transmission and grid reform provisions are very positive. And the changes that they secured in the manager’s amendment make this a better bill. Nevertheless, the bill needs further improvement before I can support it. “My top priorities in such an agreement are to bring down energy bills through new clean energy development, to lower emission rates, to support tribal sovereignty, and to stop the administration from attacking American clean energy projects. This includes restoring the billions of dollars in terminated energy projects in California, as well as the offshore wind projects the administration baselessly and illegally canceled. The president’s comments today, that notwithstanding any compromise in this bill, he intends to continue blocking wind projects, demonstrate a singular but telling lack of good faith. I have said from the start that we need to have confidence that any permitting reform legislation is not going to be weaponized by this or any future administration to single out states and provide giveaways to the oil and gas industries. In its current form, this bill does not satisfy those priorities and raises other serious concerns. “This legislation would jeopardize tribal sovereignty through major changes to the National Historic Preservation Act , impact the State of California’s authorities under the Clean Water Act , and constrict federal agencies’ ability to protect vulnerable wildlife under the Endangered Species Act . While I support the provisions in this bill that require data center companies to cover the costs of grid infrastructure and protect American taxpayers from footing the bill — which mirror my legislation — the legislation overall contains too many giveaways to oil and gas with insufficient constraints on an energy policy that has prioritized corporate profit over the pocketbooks of hard-working Americans and public health. Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) introduced legislation to transfer 847 acres of federal land from the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) into trust for the Barona Band of Mission Indians. Representative Darrell Issa (R-Calif.-48) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives. The Barona Band of Mission Indians is a federally recognized Tribe in San Diego County, which was forced out of their first federally established reservation when the City of San Diego bought a portion of the Capitan Grande Reservation from the federal government to build a reservoir. After the reservation was flooded, the Tribe purchased the Barona property to create their current reservation. The Barona Tribe and the Viejas Band of Kumeyaay Indians also share a joint-trust patent to jointly manage the remaining 15,000 acres of the Capitan Grande Reservation surrounding the reservoir. The proposed parcels in the bill are adjacent to the existing 7,500-acre Barona Indian Reservation near Ramona in San Diego County and have deep cultural and historical significance to the Tribe. Adding this land into trust would connect land between the Barona Indian Reservation and the Capitan Grande Reservation. The bill would preserve existing rights-of-way, public recreational access and public trails, emergency access for federal personnel, and existing water rights and service agreements. “I am proud to join Senator Padilla in introducing legislation that will restore historical and ancestral land to the Barona Band of Mission Indians who have fought to regain their land after being pushed out,” said Senator Schiff . “This commonsense legislation is a pivotal step in supporting tribal conservation and cultural preservation.” “The Barona Band of Mission Indians have consistently fought to unify their ancestral home — and it’s past time we restore and reunify their lands to protect and preserve their sacred sites,” said Senator Padilla . “My bill would transfer over 840 acres of federal land to connect the Barona Indian Reservation and the Capitan Grande Reservation and better protect sacred sites, traditional use areas, and cultural resources on ancestral land.” “For generations, our people have been separated from the lands that hold our history, our ceremonies, and our sacred places. Today, that separation begins to end. This legislation is the bridge to Capitan Grande, a land bridge that reconnects Barona with our ancestral home,” said Barona Chairman Raymond Welch . “We are grateful to Senator Alex Padilla, Senator Adam Schiff, and Congressman Darrell Issa for listening to our people and working together across the aisle to make this possible. By placing this land in trust, they have honored our past and strengthened our future.” Last year, Schiff and Padilla announced a trio of bipartisan, bicameral bills to promote Tribal management of over 2,000 acres of land in California by transferring federal land to the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, the Pit River Tribe, and the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians. In 2024, the Senate passed of a pair of Padilla’s bills to support the restoration of Tribal lands for the Jamul Indian Village and the Lytton Rancheria of California, the first of which became law. Full text of the bill is available here . ###

Senators write: “…The definitions proposed by the SNPRM [Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking] would remove federal protections for 80 percent of streams in the United States and 95 percent of individual wetlands, which makes a mockery of the congressional intent behind the Clean Water Act.” Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works’ Fisheries, Water, and Wildlife Subcommittee, and Ed Markey (D-Mass.) are calling on the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) to abandon their new proposal that threatens to harm public health and leave communities vulnerable to flooding and loss of access to clean drinking water. The EPA’s new proposal to revise the definition of the Waters of the United States (WOTUS) rule replaces the proposed November 2025 standard with an even more extreme one, defining “relatively permanent” to mean “perennial” waters, stripping federal protections for hundreds of bodies of waters. Previously, in January 2026, the Senators urged the agencies to reverse this proposal. “As we explained then, excluding these waters from federal protection threatens drinking water, increases downstream pollution and flood risk, and shifts substantial costs onto states, communities, and ratepayers. We are disappointed that your agencies have not only chosen to disregard all of these concerns, but have put out a second, more extreme proposal that does even more harm. We urge you to abandon this effort altogether and remember your statutory responsibilities to protect drinking water, public health, and the environment,” the Senators wrote in a letter to the EPA. EPA’s latest proposal goes further to eliminate safeguards on bodies of waters that were already reduced by the Supreme Court’s 2023 decision in Sackett v. EPA. Additionally, the Senators raise concern with the subsequent harms this proposal will have on state and tribes’ capacity to manage waters, as well as on American households, who will bear the financial costs. “…Pollution does not respect the arbitrary boundaries laid out in these proposals. When upstream waters lose federal protection, downstream communities do not cease experiencing their effects of that loss…the costs of additional pollution, degraded drinking water sources and the associated health risks, diminished flood protection, and lost aquatic habitat are shifted to states, Tribes, municipalities, water utilities, and ultimately the American taxpayer,” the Senators wrote. “The Clean Water Act was enacted to “restore and maintain the chemical, physical, and biological integrity of the Nation’s waters.” Proposing to systematically exclude waters known to be critical to that integrity ignores science and defeats the purpose of the Act…We urge you to abandon this disastrous SNPRM as well as the 2025 proposal and leave the 2023 conforming rule in place,” the Senators concluded. The EPW Committee’s Ranking Member, U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), also signed the letter. The full text of the letter can be found here and below. Dear Administrator Zeldin and Mr. Forsgren: We write to express our serious concern regarding the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ September 9, 2026 Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (SNPRM) that proposes to further narrow which waters would receive federal protections under the Clean Water Act. On January 28, 2026, we urged the agencies to abandon the proposed 2025 waters of the United States (WOTUS) rule. As we explained then, excluding these waters from federal protection threatens drinking water, increases downstream pollution and flood risk, and shifts substantial costs onto states, communities, and ratepayers. We are disappointed that your agencies have not only chosen to disregard all of these concerns, but have put out a second, more extreme proposal that does even more harm. We urge you to abandon this effort altogether and remember your statutory responsibilities to protect drinking water, public health, and the environment. The core proposal of the SNPRM is to define “relatively permanent” waters to include only perennial waters, which the proposal suggests defining as “having standing or continuously flowing water every day of the year during ordinary conditions.” The SNPRM includes limited exceptions for drought, dry spells, and low tides, and allows only a single interruption of no more than 30 consecutive days annually. The SNPRM also considers a definition of “continuous surface connection” that would require even perennial surface water within a wetland to be continuously connected to a jurisdictional water in order to merit protection as WOTUS. Limiting “relatively permanent” waters to perennial and interconnected waters would be scientifically indefensible and would put downstream water quality at risk. EPA’s own scientific record demonstrates why. EPA’s review of more than 1,200 peer-reviewed studies concluded that streams are connected to downstream waters regardless of their size or frequency of flow and strongly influence downstream physical, chemical, and biological conditions. That review, and numerous other independent scientific studies, found that perennial, intermittent, and ephemeral tributaries transport water, sediment, nutrients, contaminants, organic material, and organisms through river networks and collectively affect larger downstream waters. Further, the definitions proposed by the SNPRM would remove federal protections for 80 percent of streams in the United States and 95 percent of individual wetlands, which makes a mockery of the congressional intent behind the Clean Water Act. Your agencies acknowledge these concerns in the SNPRM and recognize the functions served by ephemeral streams. The agencies also acknowledge that the majority of wetlands would not satisfy the supplemental definition of “continuous surface connection,” because most wetlands do not contain perennial surface water. Even more, your agencies concede that the 30-day threshold is not “scientifically-grounded” and is proposed only because it is “easy to administer.” Given these acknowledgements, it appears the entirety of the SNPRM is contradictory— proposing changes that go against the very scientific findings cited in the notice. “Easy to administer” does not justify the neglect of waterways that contribute on average 55% of the water found in larger rivers – the protection of which is the mission of your agencies and the Clean Water Act. The SNPRM also includes an arbitrary five-year cutoff for waters impacted by drought conditions, a policy that would cause particular harm to more arid regions like the West. After five years of dry conditions, such drought conditions would be treated as the new baseline. As American Rivers explains in its public comment, this would “convert a growing share of currently ‘relatively permanent’ waters to non-jurisdictional status over time, particularly in the West, as droughts lengthen and recur more frequently.” The agencies justify these contradictions and known harms in part by claiming that the proposal allegedly provides regulatory clarity, giving landowners clearer notice of Clean Water Act obligations. But administrative simplicity cannot provide cover for a scientifically and legally indefensible interpretation of the Clean Water Act, as its primary purpose is to protect waters from pollution. Moreover, this SNPRM would not provide clarity, as it would inevitably lead to litigation and overwhelm state and tribal capacity to manage waters. The agencies acknowledge in the supplemental proposal that “Tribes may disproportionately rely on the Federal Government for water program implementation and enforcement of water quality violations” and “many Tribes are still building capacity and may lack resources to create a Tribal water program.” This SNPRM will remove federal protections for many waters Tribes may care about, thus pulling the rug out from under them. As we emphasized in January, pollution does not respect the arbitrary boundaries laid out in these proposals. When upstream waters lose federal protection, downstream communities do not cease experiencing their effects of that loss. And states are not going to be able to fill the gaps left by the SNPRM. One state’s hypothetical capacity to regulate their own waters, absent federal law, does not mean as much when an under-resourced, upstream state exports the cost of their water quality remediation downstream. Instead, the costs of additional pollution, degraded drinking water sources and the associated health risks, diminished flood protection, and lost aquatic habitat are shifted to states, Tribes, municipalities, water utilities, and ultimately the American taxpayer. Our previous letter warned that narrowing WOTUS in this manner would transfer responsibility and costs downstream rather than eliminate them. The recent supplemental proposal fails to heed that warning and would multiply these costs to the American people. The Clean Water Act was enacted to “restore and maintain the chemical, physical, and biological integrity of the Nation’s waters.” Proposing to systematically exclude waters known to be critical to that integrity ignores science and defeats the purpose of the Act. Although we do not agree with its reasoning, the Supreme Court spoke in Sackett v. EPA, and EPA and the Corps conformed to that decision in 2023. There is no need for a further rulemaking, especially when that rulemaking envisions slashing federal water protections even further than the Supreme Court already has. The SNPRM your agencies have published includes a litany of contradictions and acknowledged significant harm to human health and the environment. We urge you to abandon this disastrous SNPRM as well as the 2025 proposal and leave the 2023 conforming rule in place. ###

Washington, D.C. — Earlier this week, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) announced that six California projects will receive more than $116 million in federal funding through President Biden’s Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), which Padilla and Schiff voted to pass. The funding, awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Program, will improve railroad crossing safety, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen rail infrastructure in Burlingame, Sunnyvale, Richmond, Riverside, San Diego, and Suisun City. “I am proud to help deliver federal funding for critical safety and modernization upgrades for railroad crossings throughout California—made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law . All Californians deserve to live in communities with robust transportation infrastructure that helps reduce congestion. These federal investments will help ensure the safety of our pedestrians and drivers,” said Senator Schiff. “These federal investments will help make California’s railroad crossings safer, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen the transportation infrastructure our communities depend on,” said Senator Padilla. “From eliminating hazardous crossings to planning future safety upgrades, these projects will improve mobility for Californians and support a stronger regional economy thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law . I’ll keep fighting to ensure our communities get these critical investments and the resources they need to grow and thrive.” The six California projects selected for funding will advance grade separation projects, feasibility studies, and planning efforts to improve safety and mobility for motorists, pedestrians, cyclists, and rail passengers. Burlingame Broadway Grade Separation Project — $90.42 million: The Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board will eliminate an at-grade crossing by constructing an elevated rail structure and lowering the roadway, improving safety and reducing traffic delays. Mary Avenue Grade Separation Project, Sunnyvale — $15.50 million: The City of Sunnyvale will advance final design work for a future grade separation along the Caltrain corridor. Cutting/Carlson At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study, Richmond — $3.36 million: The City of Richmond will plan for a future grade separation at the Cutting Boulevard crossing along the Union Pacific Railroad corridor. Spruce Street Crossing Closure and Grade Separation Project, Riverside — $2.80 million: The City of Riverside will advance planning and project development for a future grade separation along the BNSF corridor. San Diego Regionwide At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study — $2.73 million: The San Diego Association of Governments (SANDAG) will plan for safety improvements, separations, or elimination of 39 grade crossings across the regional rail network. Sunset Avenue Grade Separation Feasibility Study, Suisun City — $2.01 million: The City of Suisun City will evaluate alternatives to separate vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian traffic from the Union Pacific Railroad corridor. ###

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) joined U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), and Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) in a letter to X (formerly Twitter) Chief Compliance Officer C. Rob DeCampos requesting answers on the seemingly preferential treatment Polymarket is receiving from X. The Senators raise concern that, due to Donald Trump Jr.’s role as an adviser and investor for Polymarket, any preferential treatment could help the President and his family enrich themselves. “Typically, X allows users to report an ad for a myriad of reasons; however, when attempting to report Polymarket’s ads through the standard X interface, users are denied the option to do so (Figure A). This is not the case with other types of advertisements, including Kalshi, another prediction markets platform offering sports gaming that is illegal in states across the U.S.,” the Senators wrote. “This seemingly preferential treatment calls into question whether X is attempting to provide an undue competitive advantage to Polymarket and – by extension – the President and his family,” the Senators continued. “It would not be the first time Donald Trump Jr. has attempted to use his position to enrich himself. Earlier this year, he reportedly pressured a room of Republican state attorneys general to stop trying to regulate prediction markets, which he is heavily invested in.” The full text of the letter can be found here and below. Dear Mr. DeCampos, We bring to your immediate attention concerns that X, formerly known as Twitter, may be giving preferential treatment to Polymarket, a prediction market platform offering illegal sports gambling across the United States. It has been widely reported that Donald Trump Jr., President Donald Trump’s eldest son, is an adviser to and investor in Polymarket. Providing preferential treatment to a specific advertiser with direct financial ties to the President and his family raises significant questions. Polymarket has been advertising on television, billboards, and social media since resuming limited onshore operations last year. The platform was previously banned in the United States for operating an unregistered derivatives-trading platform and has been the subject of increased scrutiny for enabling fraud and for allowing insider trading that could endanger military operations and national security. Since the start of the year, Polymarket has also been the subject of lawsuits by state attorneys general for facilitating illegal sports gaming. Since 1961, the Federal Wire Act has prohibited the transmission of bets or wagers through interstate commerce (18 U.S. Code § 1084) and Section 5c(c)(5)(C) of the Commodity Exchange Act permits the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to prohibit event contracts that involve gaming, are unlawful under federal or state law, or are contrary to the public interest. Despite that, sports wagers on prediction markets – deemed illegal by both the Ninth and Sixth Circuit Courts – make up more than 80 percent of Polymarket’s trading volume and are the primary source of the platform’s rapid growth. Polymarket’s X ads target new users with videos featuring sports betting services and offering financial incentives to create an account. Typically, X allows users to report an ad for a myriad of reasons; however, when attempting to report Polymarket’s ads through the standard X interface, users are denied the option to do so (Figure A). This is not the case with other types of advertisements, including Kalshi, another prediction markets platform offering sports gaming that is illegal in states across the U.S., including in Nevada (Figure B). This seemingly preferential treatment calls into question whether X is attempting to provide an undue competitive advantage to Polymarket and – by extension – the President and his family. It would not be the first time Donald Trump Jr. has attempted to use his position to enrich himself. Earlier this year, he reportedly pressured6 a room of Republican state attorneys general to stop trying to regulate prediction markets, which he is heavily invested in. Given the need to eliminate even the appearance of impropriety, we request the answers to the following questions: Does X allow advertisers to purchase ads that cannot be reported through X’s timeline interface? If so, which advertisers does X provide this service to? If so, how much additional revenue does X receive for providing this service? If so, does X receive any preferential treatment from advertisers or regulators for offering this service? Did Polymarket, its leadership, or any of its representatives approach X about running ads with a limited report function? If so, who? Did President Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., or any other member or representative of the Trump family approach X about running ads with a limited report function? If so, who? How does X plan to ensure prediction market ads featuring sports are banned from the platform in states following the Sixth and Ninth Circuit decisions that sports event contracts are sports gaming and must be regulated at the state and Tribal levels? Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both-D-Calif.), members of the Senate Judiciary Committee, released the following statements following recent oversight of big tech social media companies’ efforts to combat election disinformation and misinformation. “Social media companies hold enormous power over the content voters see. Americans’ right to vote shouldn’t be undermined by deceptive election information online like false dates, locations, times, and methods for voting. And it is platforms’ responsibility to address inaccurate content where it exists. In recent days, my staff has met with representatives of these companies to hear about their efforts to tackle false content about our elections and to combat this danger to our democracy, and I appreciate the efforts some of the companies are taking to help prevent foreign election influence operations. However, it appears that not every company is taking seriously the false information online about voting – which in some cases continues to be disseminated by the Trump Administration with the intention to interfere with our election system. I will continue pressing for commitments where they should do more, including by acting on their existing policies to remove false content about voting,” said Senator Schiff. “The Trump Administration has gutted efforts to protect voters from election interference, but social media companies still have a responsibility to combat election mis- and disinformation. So far, their responses are incomplete and raise serious questions about who’s protecting American elections from malign influence operations. Social media companies must take concrete steps to identify and address false claims about voting, shut down foreign influence operations, and enforce their policies consistently. With the midterms underway, I’ll keep pressing for answers and meaningful action to protect voters and our democracy,” said Senator Padilla . Background: On October 1, 2026, Senators Schiff and Padilla pressed the top executives of the largest social media companies about their plans to combat misinformation and disinformation on their platforms ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The Senators requested answers on the companies’ policies to identify and respond to election mis and disinformation, what actions they will be taking for the 2026 midterm elections, the steps to ensure that the Supreme Court’s mail-in ballot ruling is not subject to mis- and disinformation campaigns that undermine the integrity of mail-in voting, and whether they’ve received requests from the Trump admin relating to election security. Following their inquiry over the past month, staff from the Senators’ offices met with companies to obtain more information about their plans, and what more must be done ahead of the upcoming election. ###

Long Beach, CA – Earlier this week, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) spoke at the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) California-Hawaii State Convention, where he warned that the achievements of the civil rights era are under attack by the Trump administration. During his address, Schiff condemned Republicans’ assault on voting rights including the Supreme Court’s weakening of the Voting Rights Act , President Trump’s election denial and voter fraud conspiracies, and Republicans’ push to pass the SAVE Act in Congress, which would put millions of Americans at risk of losing their ability to vote. “To the bigotry and the hate, we must say, we will not be deterred. When they close the polling places on Sunday, we vote on Saturday. We will not be deterred. When they close the polling place near our homes, we will find another. We will not be deterred. When they illegally purge us from the voter rolls, we will re-register. We will not be deterred,” Senator Schiff said during his address. Schiff pledged to fight disenfranchisement and bigotry at every turn by pushing to restore the Voting Rights Act and Americans’ civil rights protections. Read the transcript of his remarks as delivered below: Thank you, Reverend Butler and President Callender, for welcoming me here today. Thank you all for inviting me. Thank you for being here, to the many branches of NAACP across California and Hawaii. Thank you for making the journey here today. I’m so grateful to have this moment to speak with you at such a critical time in the history of our democracy and of our country. First of all, my congratulations to the award recipients today, and thank you for your extraordinary work. These awards are named for three great Californians, three great champions of prosperity, equality, and dignity in our great American experiment. I knew Ruby McKnight Williams’ legacy very well after serving in the House of Representatives representing Pasadena for so many years. A woman whose passion for justice was forged by her own experience with discrimination, like the denial of her own employment when she was told she could not be hired as a teacher in Pasadena because of the color of her skin. That passion led her to shape the community we know today by fighting for fair and equal opportunity for employment, for home ownership, and for access to public facilities. Lulann Sapp McGriff was a champion for school integration and better resources for Black students in San Francisco for nearly her entire adult life. As her longtime friend told it, she fielded calls sometimes more than 200 a day to her NAACP office, asking for her leadership in addressing issues at local schools and in the community. She crisscrossed the nation to fight for the disenfranchised, the economically disadvantaged, the targets of prejudice and discrimination. And Willis Edwards, the former President of the Beverly Hills and Hollywood branch, whose life took him from the roads of the Kaweah Indian Reservation in Palm Springs to the side of Robert F. Kennedy during his presidential campaign, and the good Robert F. Kennedy, not the crazy brainworm addle version of Robert F. Kennedy, and later to Jesse Jackson’s campaign in 1988, a man whose dedication and devotion to elevating Black excellence saw him fight successfully to bring the Image Awards to national television, and whose dedication held fast even as he fought the stigma of HIV/AIDS. In the face of discrimination, of disinterest, of disease, and devastating odds, these three leaders stood tall, through withering attacks, and succeeded, and today three more names joined them, adding to the broader legacy of NAACP by fighting for a society that lives up to this country’s elusive promise. This recognition is more important now than ever, for it is no exaggeration to say that we find ourselves in a moment where the achievements of the past are under fresh assault, when we must fight a retrenching battle to preserve the accomplishments of the civil rights era, when events happen daily that we thought were a thing of the permanent past, and when bigotry again has become the official policy of the administration. We have seen a White House so obsessed with the conspiracies of election denial and voter fraud that they’ve turned to the very tools of the civil rights era that we had hoped to put to rest: purges of voter rolls, implementation of restrictive voting laws, with new and extreme voter ID laws, all coupled with threats to cut off funding or worse, if states do not comply. We’ve seen the Supreme Court of the United States take a hatchet to the Voting Rights Act, dismantling the protections against discrimination and the safeguards of representation, and putting Black communities, most particularly in the South, at risk of losing their voices in our democracy. And too many states have seized on the new administration’s embrace of bigotry, to close down polling places in urban centers, to close down voting on Sundays so as to thwart people from going from the pews to the polls, to take aim at Black voters and tell them in so many deeds, if not words, your vote is not welcome, not wanted, not desired, not possible. For months and months, the president has pushed the greatest disenfranchisement effort of the 21st century, the so-called SAVE Act, designed to save nothing more than a deeply unpopular president and his unpopular majority by getting Congress to pass legislation that would amount to a restoration of a new version of Jim Crow laws, putting 21 million people at risk of losing their ability to vote. Americans who don’t have a passport, or who have changed their name when they got married, or who don’t have access to their birth certificate, cut off from the right to vote. We have seen the Civil Rights Division of the Justice Department deformed into a perverse mockery of itself, a kind of anti-Civil Rights Division, one that turns the rhetoric, the history, and the legacy of anti-discrimination work on its head to attack the very goals it once sought to achieve, where a school or university seeking equity or diversity or God forbid, inclusion for historically disenfranchised and disadvantaged communities is now under assault, accused of racism by a DOJ which has now embraced racism. It is a world turned on its side, where up is down, wrong is right, and there is no black and white, no room for black, only white. Where refugees are turned away from every country, most particularly countries in Africa or countries whose people are dark-skinned, and only white Afrikaners are embraced. Where the president has a particular name, a particular epithet for countries that do not share his skin color, which oddly enough is a peculiar shade of orange. Or take our Department of Defense, where Pete Hegseth has embraced and embarked so fully on his mission against DEI that he not only saw the first Black chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff fired, but he also has made a habit of blocking the promotions of Black and female officer candidates, as if being Black or a woman or up for promotion now means simply you cannot have earned that rank on your own merit. And throughout the federal government, the administration is taking pains to erase our history, your history, from government websites and museums, from parks and from schools. And what does the Supreme Court do amidst this unconstitutional wave of state-sponsored bigotry? What does the court, which once decided Brown v. Board of Education, do? It defiles itself by blessing ICE’s strategy to consider the color of your skin, the language that you speak, the place where you congregate to be probable cause enough to see you detained, our government has recruited the worst cultures of Jim Crow. Millions in this country today are afraid to leave their house, walk down their street, take their kids to school or to go to their place of work or worship. Millions of citizens fear being stopped and asked for their papers, for their papers in their own country. This is what generations before us marched against throughout the South and much of the North, across the Edmund Pettus Bridge, and in 1000 other places, and it is a challenge that we now face. A challenge that is being met by this community, and by leaders like Maxine Waters. For the Black community has responded, showing up in record numbers to vote early, and ensure that their voices will be heard, that they will not be silenced, will not go back, not to the back of the bus, not to the back of the line, not to a country without the right to vote. To the bigotry and the hate, we must say, we will not be deterred. When they close the polling places on Sunday, we vote on Saturday. We will not be deterred. When they close the polling place near our homes, we will find another. We will not be deterred. When they illegally purge us from the voter rolls, we will re-register. We will not be deterred. When our neighbors are afraid to take their kids to school, we will take them ourselves. We will not be deterred. When they try to normalize racism, when they try to make our fellow citizens feel small, when they try to make our neighbors feel less and unsafe, we will speak out. We will push back. We will not be deterred. I have had many privileges in my career as a public servant, but few that I cherish as much as my friendship with John Lewis, a man who embodied the phrase “walk the walk.” I had the chance many years ago to walk with John on the anniversary of Bloody Sunday across the Edmund Pettus Bridge to the place where John was almost beaten to death. The site, not just of struggle but also of inspiration, because for every swing of the club that John Lewis and other civil rights leaders endured that day, 10 times that number, 1000 times that number, were inspired to join them in their struggle. But here’s what I found most inspiring about working with John. He saw the great achievements of the civil rights movement, because he was a part of them. But he also lived long enough to see the great periods of setback, of backpedaling, and relapse, and through all of those times of difficulty and disappointment, times when I was at risk, and I know others the same, of falling into a kind of despair. John was there to lift me up, to lift all of us up on those broad shoulders. For I never saw John have a bad day. Never saw him less than hopeful about the future of our country, and I would think to myself, if John Lewis, after seeing all that he has seen, all that he has experienced, can be optimistic about the future, well then so can I, and I am. We will get through this. This too shall pass. But what we do in this moment will determine how quickly it passes, and how much damage we are forced to suffer along the way. John once said, “Ours is not the struggle of one day, one week, or one year. Ours is not the struggle of one judicial appointment or presidential term. Ours is the struggle of a lifetime and maybe even many lifetimes.” And each one of us, in every generation, must do our part. Those who are earning the awards bestowed on them by the NAACP today are doing their part. I’m committed to doing mine. To fight these disenfranchisement efforts at every turn. To restore the Voting Rights Act. And to do so in John Lewis’s name. To restore the Civil Rights Division in a future administration to one that respects the name and the legacy of that department. To hold the Hegseths and the Vosses and the Blanches and all of the other miscreants to account, including the one who now holds and makes odious the title of president. And to continue to work with community leaders like you to chart the best path forward to a stronger and more prosperous nation in the years and decades to come. We will not be deterred. We will not back down from these necessary fights or shirk our responsibility. We will put a stop to the erosion of rights that others have labored and died to protect. We will not allow the wealthiest and the most powerful in this country to decide for all of us who will govern and which laws they will deign to follow. We will ensure that our children, born into the wealthiest nation in the history of the world, are not afforded fewer opportunities than we were. We are the custodians of the promise of America, a promise not fully kept, but a promise worth fighting for. Ida B. Wells once said, “There must always be a remedy for wrong and injustice if we only know how to find it.” I find it here with all of you, and I thank you again for having me and for this great privilege. Thank you. ###

Fulltime Yosemite employees are losing $8,320 in annual wages from change in administration policy Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) are urging Department of the Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to reverse and restore lost compensation for maintenance and service employees at Yosemite National Park after facing pay reductions of up to $4.00 per hour as a result of a wage-area reclassification. In January 2025, the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a final rule revising the boundaries of wage areas for Federal Wage System employees – employees were moved from the San Jose-San Francisco-Oakland pay locality to the new Fresno-Madera-Hanford wage area, which resulted in significant pay cuts. While 85% of Federal Wage System employees impacted by these changes received raises, Yosemite employees did not receive pay retention and faced immediate loss in compensation. “It is unclear to us why Yosemite employees have been left out in the cold…Yosemite is already experiencing substantial operational strain, staffing losses, and risks of facility closures. Reducing compensation for skilled Federal Wage System employees will further impair the National Park Service’s ability to recruit and retain the workforce necessary to maintain the park’s facilities, protect natural resources, and ensure visitor safety,” the Senators wrote. “Further, the loss of experienced tradespeople with specialized institutional and technical knowledge could further undermine Yosemite’s ability to maintain critical infrastructure and sustain park operations,” the Senators continued. The Senators are demanding the Department of the Interior provide answers on what steps they are taking to restore lost compensation, how many FWS employees at Yosemite National Park experienced a reduction in pay, why the Yosemite employees who were reclassified under the Fresno pay locality are not eligible for pay retention, and if this issue has been brought to the Federal Prevailing Rate Advisory Committee or OPM. The full text of the letter can be found here and below. Dear Secretary Burgum: We write to share concerns regarding the significant pay cuts experienced by maintenance and service employees at Yosemite National Park and ask that DOI take immediate action to address these pay cuts. On January 21, 2025, the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a final rule revising the regulatory criteria used to define Federal Wage System wage areas and modifying the boundaries of certain wage areas. This rule was intended to better align Federal Wage System boundaries with General Schedule (GS) locality pay areas and was supposed to better reflect current commuting, employment, and recruitment patterns. The rule took effect in October 2025, and has been implemented in rolling phases, resulting in changes to wage-area designations nationwide. Despite the intent of the rule, we are concerned how the rule has affected the employees responsible for maintaining Yosemite National Park and keeping it safe for the visiting public. Changes affecting Yosemite’s Federal Wage System employees took place in January 2026. Prior to these changes, employees at Yosemite were grouped with the San Jose-San Francisco-Oakland pay locality. The reclassification moved the national park into the new Fresno-Madera-Hanford wage area, resulting in significant pay cuts for the maintenance workers, trail crews, mechanics, and painters employed by the park. Some workers experienced reductions of up to $4 per hour, with higher-wage employees facing even larger cuts. For an employee working 40 hours per week, a $4 per hour reduction amounts to approximately $8,320 in lost annual wages. Unlike other federal employees affected by the rule, Yosemite employees did not receive pay retention from DOI and therefore experienced immediate reductions in their compensation. This is deeply unfair, given that 85 percent of federal employees affected by the new rule received pay increases, while 11 percent received pay retention to protect them from pay cuts. It is unclear to us why Yosemite employees have been left out in the cold. The Fresno wage area does not adequately reflect the cost of living around Yosemite National Park. Many Yosemite employees already commute significant distances to reach the park, and further reductions in compensation risk worsening existing recruitment and retention challenges at the national park. Yosemite is already experiencing substantial operational strain, staffing losses, and risks of facility closures. Reducing compensation for skilled Federal Wage System employees will further impair the National Park Service’s ability to recruit and retain the workforce necessary to maintain the park’s facilities, protect natural resources, and ensure visitor safety. Further, the loss of experienced tradespeople with specialized institutional and technical knowledge could further undermine Yosemite’s ability to maintain critical infrastructure and sustain park operations. In December 2025, a Department spokesperson stated, “We are coordinating with the Office of Human Capital to understand the impacts and to identify options that may help affected employees.” The Department has had months to act, but it appears that DOI has not taken any meaningful action to protect Yosemite’s employees from pay cuts, even though the final rule from OPM noted that “federal agencies have considerable discretionary authority to provide pay and leave flexibilities to address significant recruitment and retention problems.” To understand the impacts to the workers at Yosemite and the steps you are taking to protect them, we request responses to the following no later than November 11, 2026: What actions is the Department of the Interior taking, or considering taking, to restore lost compensation or otherwise make affected Yosemite employees whole? How many Federal Wage System employees at Yosemite National Park experienced a reduction in pay as a result of the January 2026 wage-area reclassification? Please provide the number of employees and their reductions in hourly compensation. Why were the Yosemite employees who were reclassified under the Fresno pay locality not eligible for pay retention? Has DOI or NPS brought this issue to the attention of the Federal Prevailing Rate Advisory Committee or OPM? Thank you for your consideration. ###

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) issued the following statement after the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced their new proposal to weaken limits on emissions of methane and other pollutants: “First, the administration delayed compliance with pollution restrictions on methane and other chemicals, and now they are doing away with these protections altogether. This will give oil and gas companies a free pass to clog our lungs, make the air we breathe dirtier and more harmful and supercharge the risk of wildfires. “All accountability for corporate polluters is being stripped away. And the health of the American people is the cost. The EPA has abandoned its mission to protect our environment. That’s why I’ve helped to lead the fight in the Senate to stop this very action – warning that more air pollution brings more cancer, asthma, wildfires, flooding, and other public health concerns. And that’s why I will continue fighting to stop the dismantling of decades of work to curb pollution, invest in scientific solutions, and put fighting climate change ahead of serving corporate profits.” Background: Last year, Schiff and U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) introduced a resolution under the Congressional Review Act that would strike down the EPA’s extension given to oil and gas companies to avoid limits on emissions of methane and other pollutants without public input. The Senators’ resolution failed a procedural vote 46-51 in November. Most recently, Schiff joined Whitehouse in introducing the No Passes for Polluters Act , legislation to clarify congressional intent in exempting toxic polluters from regulation under the Clean Air Act. ###

Trump Administration Has Ignored Legal Deadline to Release Surveillance Court Opinion on FISA Section 702 Warrantless Surveillance Program Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) joined Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) in demanding that the Trump administration stop violating federal law and immediately declassify a surveillance court opinion that details abuses by the government of warrantless surveillance under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA). The opinion by the FISA Court was signed on March 17, 2026, and was legally required to be declassified within 180 days, on September 13. Yet the Trump administration, in violation of federal law, has still not made the opinion public. This opinion includes details about “serious abuses of Americans’ rights” that must be made public before the Senate debates reauthorizing FISA Section 702 surveillance, the Senators wrote. “As Congress continues to debate the fate of this authority, lawmakers must be able to discuss these abuses openly,” Schiff and Wyden wrote. “Otherwise, the American people will rightly question whether a government that so flagrantly violates basic legal requirements, like the statute requiring declassification, can ever be trusted to not abuse a powerful surveillance tool like Section 702.” The Senators demanded that the administration release the opinion as soon as possible and identify the officials responsible for withholding its timely release by November 6, 2026. FISA Section 702 is a powerful surveillance authority that allows the government to collect communications of foreign intelligence targets without a warrant. However, the program also sweeps up a significant amount of Americans’ communications in the process, with little oversight of impact on Americans and lawful permanent residents, making transparency about abuses particularly important. Both the chair and vice-chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee have called for the opinion to be released, and Attorney General Todd Blanche repeatedly committed to declassify the opinion by the legal deadline. The full text of the letter can be found here and below. Dear Director Clayton and Attorney General Blanche: We write to demand the administration stop violating the law and finally release a declassified version of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) opinion and order, dated March 17, 2026. This opinion details serious abuses of Americans’ rights under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) and, by law, should have been released before September 13. Yet this opinion remains hidden over a month later, suggesting that the administration hopes to secure a renewal of Section 702 while keeping Congress and the public in the dark. As Congress continues to debate the fate of this authority, lawmakers must be able to discuss these abuses openly. Otherwise, the American people will rightly question whether a government that so flagrantly violates basic legal requirements, like the statute requiring declassification, can ever be trusted to not abuse a powerful surveillance tool like Section 702. This year, Congress has on multiple occasions debated whether to extend Section 702, and ultimately let it expire in June. Despite its expiration, the administration is still permitted to continue collection under Section 702 until March 2027. This is because the March 17, 2026 FISC opinion that detailed abuses of the program also permitted the administration to continue this surveillance for another year. As such, Congress will doubtlessly debate whether to revive Section 702 in the coming months. We have long called for reforms to this program and other government surveillance. As you know, Congress continues to consider reforms to Section 702, including whether to require a warrant to search 702 collections for the communications of particular Americans, stopping the government from warrantlessly buying Americans’ data from data brokers, and limiting the people and entities that the government can conscript into surveillance of Americans. We and others have repeatedly called for the administration to release the March FISC opinion. In May, the Chair and Vice Chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee sent a letter to the administration stating their expectation that the opinion would be released by May 15 “in order to inform the Senate debate on section 702.” The statute itself requires the administration to release a declassified version of the opinion within 180 days. In July, Attorney General Blanche told the Senate Judiciary Committee he expected that the public release would happen “in advance of the statutory deadline.” Attorney General Blanche unequivocally committed to “declassifying the opinion by the statutory deadline of 180 days and complying with the law.” Nevertheless, it is now a month past the statutory deadline and the opinion has still not been released. Simply put, this is not acceptable, especially as this administration restarts its attempts to lobby Congress to renew Section 702 without reforms. The administration has now had over seven months to declassify and release this opinion. It is time to stop violating the law and finally release this opinion. And if this administration won’t follow this simple statutory directive, it is unclear why Congress or the American people should trust this administration to follow any of the other legal limits to Section 702. We demand that you release this opinion as soon as possible. We also request that you respond in writing by November 6, 2026, providing an explanation as to why the opinion was not released by the statutory deadline and identifying the officials that were responsible for withholding its timely release. Thank you for your attention to this important matter. ###

Los Angeles, CA – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, conducted an unannounced oversight visit of the Customs and Border Protection (CBP) facility at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) to see the conditions of the facility and treatment of detainees firsthand. The visit follows reports that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has been using holding areas in international airports to detain immigrants, including lawful permanent residents, for extended periods before transferring them to ICE facilities. Last week, Schiff conducted an oversight visit to the CBP holding facility at San Francisco International Airport (SFO). “The administration lied to the country. They said they were going to go after violent offenders, but such a substantial number of folks they’re going after have no record at all… They’re tearing families apart… They have just breeded such distrust and caused such cruelty, and of course that’s divisive. It’s intended to be divisive. That’s also part of the goal here. It’s not to bring people together. It’s not to have a humane immigration policy. It’s not to enforce the law. No, it’s to be cruel. That is really a part of the policy,” said Senator Schiff. During the visit Schiff also noted some of the differences he observed between Los Angeles and San Francisco’s airport CBP facilities, noting that, “People that are being held here are able to directly contact family members. In San Francisco, they have to ask the border patrol agents to call their family for them.There is the same lack of access to counsel, though, which is concerning. This appears to be the national policy of the Department of Homeland Security…. There’s really no opportunity to get advice of counsel, and that’s a concern.” Download b-roll from his visit here . Background : Schiff has continued to call out and conduct oversight of the Trump administration’s unlawful and cruel immigration policies. In March, Schiff led an oversight inquiry into the alarming data sharing by TSA and ICE relating to the arrest and removal of a mother and her minor child at SFO. In January 2026, Senator Schiff conducted a similar oversight visit to the ICE facility in California City, the largest immigration detention center in California, alongside U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.). In September 2026, Schiff introduced the Fairness to Freedom Act of 2026 , legislation to guarantee the right to legal representation for all individuals facing deportation or any legal immigration proceeding if they are unable to afford it. ###

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) released the following statement after the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)’s new draft evaluation of the California Coastal Management Program under the Coastal Zone Management Act (CZMA) was exposed by the Los Angeles Times . Schiff highlighted how the evaluation puts California’s ability to protect its coast and future coastal management funding in peril: “For half a century, California and the federal government have cooperated to protect our coastline. Now, further proof that this administration wants to end that partnership. “This trumped-up evaluation is the latest evidence of what I and our delegation have been warning of: that Donald Trump’s NOAA is creating a pretext to take away California’s power to manage its own shores. “If these threats are seen through, an administration that has proven to be hell-bent on reopening California to dangerous offshore drilling and other environmental hazards would get the sole jurisdiction over our golden coast. “This is a five-alarm warning to every job and industry that relies on our sandy beaches and beautiful bluffs for its livelihood. Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) urged Meta not to move forward with the implementation of recently announced Commercial Terms of Use that would require all commercial accounts using Meta platforms to grant expansive authorization to the company to deploy automated crawlers and web scrapers across their domains, including access to any content available through them. “The breadth of these updated provisions is extraordinary… Virtually every news organization, independent journalist, public figure, and commercial enterprise in the United States manages a Meta Page or utilizes the Meta Business Suite to reach their readers and customers, effectively requiring each of these entities to allow Meta to scrape their IP in service of the company’s own products,” wrote Senator Schiff. In the inquiry to Meta’s CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Schiff argued that the updated terms were “a gross abuse of Meta’s power,” noting that publishers and independent creators’ access to a dominant online platform necessary to reach consumers should not be conditioned on the uncompensated extraction of their intellectual property. Schiff also raised alarms that updated terms would harvest the proprietary reporting of local and independent news organizations without compensation to feed Meta’s commercial AI models. “Forcing publishers to choose between surrendering their off-platform IP or forfeiting a primary channel of public communication is a gross abuse of Meta’s power as a powerful platform with critical access to consumers,” Schiff continued. “Meta must not nullify federal IP protections and fair market competition through the unilateral insertion of fine print into terms of service contracts. A free, independent, and economically sustainable press, as well as a thriving creator economy, is indispensable to our country, and dominant platforms should not use market leverage to operate outside of the boundaries of fair licensing.” The Senator requested that the company outline specific steps they will take to address concerns by November 2, 2026. The full text of the letter can be found here and below. Dear Mr. Zuckerberg: I write to express serious concern regarding Meta’s updated Commercial Terms of Use, set to take effect on November 20, 2026.1 These revised terms require any entity using your platforms for commercial purposes to grant Meta expansive authorization to deploy automated crawlers and web scrapers across their domains, including access to any content available through them. I strongly urge Meta not to move forward with the implementation of these terms and to immediately halt any effort to condition platform access on the extraction of external intellectual property (IP). The breadth of these updated provisions is extraordinary. According to your terms, this policy applies to any access or use of Meta Company Products for a “business or commercial purpose,” encompassing any entity using ads or marketing messages, selling or listing products, developing apps, managing a Meta Page, or using any business product, “regardless of the entity type.”2 Virtually every news organization, independent journalist, public figure, and commercial enterprise in the United States manages a Meta Page or utilizes the Meta Business Suite to reach their readers and customers, effectively requiring each of these entities to allow Meta to scrape their IP in service of the company’s own products. By demanding the contractual right to “create test credentials to access, index, cache, analyze, collect, retrieve, or crawl” associated web domains of user companies, Meta asserts an alarming opening to bypass technical measures essential to the economic security of news organizations and subscription-based creators, including paywalls, registration gates, and digital subscriber barriers.3 Rather than restricting its terms to content directly shared or uploaded onto Meta Company Products, Meta’s contractual language gives the company unfettered access to publishers’ archives that may otherwise hold value in a competitive commercial licensing market. While Meta has reportedly negotiated commercial licensing agreements with select national media organizations, the company’s updated terms would harvest the proprietary reporting of local and independent publishers without compensation.4 Following swift public criticism, Meta reportedly removed the word “train” from its updated terms’ authorized uses of scraped data.5 However, legal experts maintain that the revised allowances, including using scraped data to “develop, improve, research, and maintain advertising and business products,” remain broad enough to encompass the training of Meta’s AI products.6 Independent newsrooms and creators should not be coerced into providing the underlying proprietary reporting or content that may be used to feed Meta’s commercial AI models – technologies capable of summarizing, competing with, and ultimately displacing the primary sources of that creative work. Meta’s verbal assurances that it will not supersede robots.txt files, which are voluntary server flags, do not appear to constitute enforceable legal protections.7 Without the insertion of specific language codifying Meta’s policy to respect robots.txt signals into the latest contractual terms, users lack any reliable means by which to protect their content. Meta’s updated terms provide no mechanism for businesses to opt out of scraping while maintaining their account presence, instead stating: “If you do not agree to the updated terms, you may stop all access or use of our Products for business or commercial purposes.”8 Forcing publishers to choose between surrendering their off-platform IP or forfeiting a primary channel of public communication is a gross abuse of Meta’s power as a powerful platform with critical access to consumers. Meta must not nullify federal IP protections and fair market competition through the unilateral insertion of fine print into terms of service contracts. A free, independent, and economically sustainable press, as well as a thriving creator economy, is indispensable to our country, and dominant platforms should not use market leverage to operate outside of the boundaries of fair licensing. I urge Meta not to move forward with the implementation of these Commercial Terms on November 20 so long as they require business organizations to grant unilateral off-platform scraping, provide explicit guarantees that external technical boundaries like paywalls and robots.txt protocols will be fully respected, and ensure that no business is forced to sacrifice its proprietary content simply to operate on your platforms. I request a response to this letter outlining the specific steps Meta will take to address these concerns and whether the company will suspend the rollout of these provisions by November 2, 2026. I look forward to reviewing your response. ###

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calf.) joined Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee Representative Gregory Meeks (D-NY-05) and U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) in demanding a clear explanation from Elon Musk, CEO of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX), about why access to the Starshield communications system was suddenly restricted for Ukrainian forces, which rely on SpaceX’s Starlink satellite system to defend civilians against Russian drones and missiles. In their letter , the lawmakers underscore that while Musk has publicly asserted that limits to the communications system’s access are “decided by the U.S. military and ultimately POTUS,” public reporting indicates that Musk personally brought the suggestion to President Trump to slow down Ukrainian communications through SpaceX’s Starlink systems. The lawmakers also highlight that U.S. government officials have reportedly indicated that Musk personally ordered a speed cap on the Ukrainian military’s use of Starshield, the military version of Starlink. Reports published on October 22, 2026, in the Wall Street Journal , indicate that President Trump called Musk to personally ask for the restoration of Starshield capabilities. While the President has asserted it has since been restored, public reports indicate the system remains severely restricted for Ukraine’s defense forces. “Since the failure of his ground invasion, Russian leader Vladimir Putin turned to a brutal air campaign targeting Ukrainian civilians to wear down public morale. Just last month, more than 300 Ukrainian civilians were killed and 2,000 injured by Russian drone and missile strikes. Ukraine has built an innovative network of drone systems to defend against the thousands of strikes launched each month by Russia. However, these life-saving systems often depend on Starlink’s military version, Starshield, for accurate communication and transmission of targeting data,” wrote the lawmakers . “Last week on October 13, 2026, Ukrainian officials said that their forces suddenly lost access to Starshield communications inside Ukraine for drones moving over 100 miles per hour. That interruption halted Ukraine’s ability to guide its self-defense drones against incoming Russian missiles and drones and stopped Ukrainian attacks against Russian positions,” the lawmakers continued . “That very night, Russia launched a record-setting coordinated drone and missile barrage at Ukrainian civilian energy infrastructure, using at least 39 ballistic and hypersonic missiles and 128 Shahed-type drones. The strikes killed at least three civilians, including a child, and injured at least 21.” The lawmakers concluded: “As a publicly traded company, SpaceX has a legal obligation to disclose to shareholders and the public material events that could affect your business model. The revelation that you personally wielded control over a foreign country’s military communications would require disclosure of elevated risks for corporate governance, geopolitical exposure, and potential adverse actions by foreign governments.” The lawmakers requested answers to the following questions by October 31, 2026: Have you or any SpaceX official at any point discussed limiting Starlink access for Ukrainian forces inside Russia or Ukraine with Russian President Vladimir Putin, President Trump, or any officials or representatives acting on their behalf? Please provide any such communications or records of communications. Did you, SpaceX, or entities operating on SpaceX’s behalf reduce, shut off, or throttle Starlink access to Ukrainian forces this month—either inside Russia or Ukraine? If so, why and on whose orders? Have you or any official at SpaceX communicated to Ukrainian officials any conditions or actions required for a full or partial resumption Starlink access for Ukrainian defense forces? Did President Trump or the White House, in fact, make a request to restore Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield systems? Have those systems been fully restored? If so, when? And if not, why not? Which specific individuals, agencies, or entities control the operational decisions from this day forward on restoring full and non-capped access to Starlink and Starshield communications systems for Ukrainian forces? The letter was also signed by Senator Michael Bennet (D-Colo.) and Reps. Jim McGovern (D-MA-02) and Rep. Jason Crow (D-CO-06). A copy of the letter is available here . ###

Schiff called for Elon Musk and senior administration officials, like Pete Hegseth, to appear under oath regarding slowdowns of Starshield in Ukraine: “Somebody is lying here…we should find out.” Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) joined NBC’s Meet the Press with Kristen Welker nine days before the 2026 midterms to highlight the biggest issues on the ballot and preview the Democratic agenda in the new Congress focused on cost of living and investigating corruption that has driven up prices for American families. Schiff, a former Department of Justice lawyer and a member of the Senate Democrats’ Election Protection Task Force, also lambasted Attorney General Todd Blanche for his complicity in helping President Donald Trump lay the groundwork to meddle in the outcome of Alaska’s upcoming Senate election – calling the DOJ’s lawsuit a “disgraceful campaign” that has “no chance of succeeding.” The Senator also called for Elon Musk and senior administration officials to appear under oath as part of a Congressional investigation into the throttling of Starshield networks in Ukraine, which rely on SpaceX’s Starlink satellite system to defend civilians against Russian drones and missiles. On Friday, Schiff and other lawmakers demanded SpaceX provide answers on the slowdown of Starshield access prior to Russian strikes that killed or wounded dozens of Ukrainians. Key Excerpts: On the dominant issue in the November 3 election: “ I do believe we can flip both houses, and for the reason that the main issue facing Americans is that their cost of living has gone up so dramatically, and a lot of it is due to the corruption that pervades this administration. An administration that is looking out for itself, making money hand over fist for the president for his family, while leaving regular families to struggle , and that is the dominant issue, and I think voters are going to turn out because their lives have not been made better by this president, and they’re going to vote accordingly. I’m proud to have played a small piece in that and brought back $1.5 million in federal funding to help the effort, but it was all of you, students and community leaders, that made this happen. Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) led a new push for answers from the White House on the recently announced gala dinner for top investors of the $TRUMP coin, the president’s latest scheme to continue using the office of the presidency to enrich himself. “President Trump’s continued monetization of his name and likeness once again raises serious ethical concerns, necessitating this request for a robust inquiry into the President’s financial entanglements and personal profiteering while costs for the American people continue to climb,” the Senators wrote.
